The vulnerability in the OnlineVotingSystem lies in the way passwords are handled. Specifically, the code directly compares plain text passwords against those stored in the database without any form of encryption or hashing.

The lack of salt in password hashing makes it vulnerable to attacks because identical passwords will produce the same hash value. This allows attackers who have access to the hashed passwords to use precomputed tables (rainbow tables) to quickly find the original passwords.

A proposed fix for this vulnerability involves using a secure hashing algorithm like bcrypt, scrypt, or Argon2, which includes a unique salt for each password. This ensures that even if two users have the same password, their hashes will be different, making rainbow table attacks ineffective.
